mutants.description: Both windows tap the blanking history at the newest end (cp_delay[0], one clock back) instead of the oldest bit cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1], so there is in effect no blanking.
mutants.reason: In S_SS or S_RUN, when cp_sync is high only in the clock just before pwm_rise (during high-side turn-on), or high 5 clocks before and low just before, the cycle is logged the opposite way, so fault_count_run_out / fault_count_ss_out and the trips change.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window is sampled at high-side turn-off (the falling edge of pwm_sync, the peak), while the soft-start window keeps using the valley at pwm_rise.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN the run window takes the blanked comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before the PWM falling edge instead of before the rising edge, so a CP pulse during the low-side period near the valley but not near the turn-off is counted wrongly in fault_count_run_out and window_trip.

mutants.description: The soft-start window records the start of an overcurrent excursion (a faulted cycle after a clear one) instead of the comparator level, so a sustained fault in S_SS is logged only on every other cycle.
mutants.reason: With cp_sync held high through S_SS, fault_count_ss_out rises at half the rate, and window_trip_SS asserts later or never (for trip_ss above 16).

mutants.description: The soft-start window takes as its sample 'cp_sync high in any of the last BLANK_CLKS clocks' instead of the one comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a CP pulse in the last few clocks before pwm_rise (inside the blanking interval) counts as a faulted cycle, so fault_count_ss_out is too high and window_trip_SS can assert early.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window counts a cycle as faulted only if the comparator was high on every clock of the blanking history (a debounce), instead of the one value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a cycle where cp_sync was high BLANK_CLKS clocks before pwm_rise but dropped in between is not counted, so fault_count_run_out is low and window_trip is missed.

mutants.description: An overflow guard stops the run count adding the entering sample once it reaches WINDOW_RUN, but the leaving bit is still subtracted, so a full window followed by another faulted cycle drops the count to 15.
mutants.reason: After more than 16 consecutive faulted cycles in S_RUN, fault_count_run_out reads 15 instead of 16 (and window_trip drops for trip_run=16); when the faults then clear the count wraps below zero to 31.

mutants.description: The soft-start count's overflow guard is compared with the run-window depth (WINDOW_RUN, 16) instead of WINDOW_SS, so the count stops adding entering samples at 16 while still subtracting leaving ones.
mutants.reason: With more than 16 faulted cycles in S_SS, fault_count_ss_out stops at 16 (then drifts lower), so window_trip_SS never asserts for a trip_ss above 16, and the count wraps when the faults leave the window.

mutants.description: The soft-start window stops sampling once its count reaches a full window (saturation applied to the whole update), so a fully faulted window is frozen instead of rolling.
mutants.reason: After 32 consecutive faulted cycles in S_SS, later clear cycles no longer reduce the count: fault_count_ss_out stays at 32 and window_trip_SS stays high for the rest of soft start.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip compares count and threshold as signed values, so a trip_run of 32 or more (top bit set) is read as a negative threshold.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with trip_run set to 32..63 (meant as 'never trip'), window_trip asserts at once with no faulted cycles.
